title: The Incomparables, Dink Johnson and band personnel
summary: Naming the Incomparable band, Jelly's feud with drummer Dink over lateness, and other members like Bynum and Woodman.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: And the Jellies band played out there.
Yeah.
That is what it's called, Incomparables or...
Incomparable.
Incomparables.
Yeah, he named it that. That's the time him and Dink fell out. I'm trying to remember the drummer we had. He wouldn't let Dink play for him no more.
What happened to him?

Well, Dink always come late and Jetta Rola was very temperamental. You know, he had to be there on time. It's all right for him to walk in. Well, I'm the boss. I don't have nothing to do. Boom. He'd stomp on me, there we go. You'd be there on time, ready to play. Dink come there and take him a half an hour to set up his drum. Yeah. I heard he passed.
Yes, about 1954 or several years ago. About four years ago in November, I think. Didn't I? Up in Portland.
Oh, he went to Portland. Yeah. He left Santa Barbara. Yeah.
Right up there. And he'd been down to Santa Barbara. And he also had a place right next to Wrigley Field there when I knew him. A little restaurant.
Yeah.
Called Dink's Place. And musicians, what do you call it? Musicians Club or something. I don't remember. Who else was in the band?
Well, I can recall a saxophone player. And he's dead. His name was Bynum. That's all I can remember. The trumpet player. He was a fucker.
Who was he doing?
He played a tenor sax. And the trumpet player was a fellow after 24th Infantry. He's dead. I can't remember his name. But he wasn't from around New Orleans or nothing.
He came up in Los Angeles.
Yeah. Let's see who. This Woodman. You met him. His son played with Duke Ellerton. He's a barber down there. He was playing trombone.
I know the name. I never remember.
Well, his young son. Well, that's the last name, Woodman. I don't even remember his first name.
He had about five pieces then.
We had six. Six. Was there a bass? Yeah, we had a bass player. But they didn't play a bass like Mount Tutti. No.
You knew Judy then pretty well.
Oh, yeah. I knew him in New Orleans.
